rule: Constructor / initializer call: `Type#<init>`. | Superclass constructor calls (`super(...)`, `: base(...)`, `: this(...)`, PHP `parent::__construct(...)`, Ruby `super` inside `initialize`) → `Parent#<init>`, constructor. | Generic/template type arguments are dropped from every ID (`HashSet#<init>`).
notes: : base(...) → Parent#<init> and : this(...) → own Type#<init>, both constructor, on the line of the base/this keyword; both Dog constructors share App.Dog#<init> (overloads). Normalize(name) is written in the constructor initializer, which is part of the constructor, so its caller is App.Dog#<init>. List<Dog> drops its type argument; the type is written fully qualified (medium). `var items = new ...List<Dog>()` types items (decision A), so items.Add is List#Add, medium. Animal's constructor body only assigns a field.
